If both `split_id` and `recorded_split` are `None`/empty (no split passed, no resolvable `current_split`, and no build-config file), `Path / None` raises `TypeError` instead of producing the ASK issue. The existing test passes only because the canon/plan-side resolution supplies a split in that fixture; the bare "no build config, no split anywhere" state isn't covered.
findings.suggestion: Guard the fallback — if `(split_id or recorded_split)` is falsy, skip the plan-side lookup (or treat it as empty) so the existing "No sections found… Did /shipwright-plan complete?" ASK path handles it.

findings.finding: The "build config wins" half doesn't actually prove precedence: writing `extra.md` and passing doesn't distinguish "build-config sections used" from "plan-side files used", since both would validate. Only the second half (adding a bogus `gone` section) demonstrates the config is consulted.
findings.suggestion: Make the first half meaningful — e.g., put a section in the config whose file does NOT exist while plan-side files do, and assert it fails; that proves plan-side files don't mask config entries.  No security or regression concerns: the fallback is read-only, scoped under `.shipwright/planning/<split>/`, and `split_id` traversal is already constrained by the earlier resolved-splits check described in the docstring. Returned section dicts (`{"name": ...}` only) are only used for the name/exists check in this validator.  Overall: implements the spec correctly with good error-path coverage; the two items above are refinements, not blockers.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve
